narrative_purpose: Makes the millionfold volume gap between a cloud droplet and a raindrop physically felt rather than merely stated - the step that diffusion cannot climb and coalescence must.
subject: A comparison plate on a plain dark ground. On one side, a single very small sphere of water, faintly glowing, isolated with generous empty space around it. On the other side, one sphere roughly a hundred times its radius, rendered as a real water drop with light refracting through it. Gathered beside and partly behind the large drop is a dense drifting field of the tiny spheres, numerous enough to read as an uncountable swarm, suggesting how many were consumed to build the one large drop.
scene: Empty dark air with no landscape, no horizon and no context - a laboratory-like void so nothing competes with the size comparison.
camera: Straight-on view at the same distance from both drops, flat and diagrammatic, no perspective foreshortening between them.
light: Single soft off-frame source; both drops lit identically so the only difference the eye reads is size. Faint internal refraction in the large drop.
palette: Deep void-indigo ground, misty-cyan water with pale highlights, faint teal in the swarm of small droplets.
style: Painterly plate with a clean comparative layout; real water rendering with soft refraction, NOT a hard vector schematic and NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: High on both drops' surfaces and the refraction in the large one; the swarm soft and unresolved so it reads as quantity rather than individuals.
composition: Two clear zones separated by empty dark space, the small drop given deliberately excessive room so its smallness registers, and generous plain background on both outer edges for callouts.
consistency_notes: Water is the same misty-cyan used for water-in-air throughout the chapter. No scale bar or measurement chrome of any kind - the comparison is carried by the drops themselves and by the caption.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no scale bar, no ruler, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look
